questions.stem: Which mission profile passes a target without entering a sustained orbit around it?
options: Surface lander
Atmospheric balloon
Orbiter
Flyby
questions.explanation: A flyby observes while following a passing trajectory; an orbiter is captured into orbit.

questions.stem: What distinguishes an orbiter from a flyby spacecraft at its target?
options: It enters an orbit around the target body
It passes the target without entering a sustained orbit
It floats and drifts through the target atmosphere
It measures the surface from a stationary landing site
questions.explanation: An orbiter enters a sustained orbit; a flyby travels past the target.

questions.stem: During solar occultation by a target body, what must a solar-powered orbiter plan for?
options: Reduced solar generation and cooling
Loss of all onboard stored data
Automatic loss of orbital capture
Permanent elimination of thermal stresses
questions.explanation: When the target blocks the Sun, solar generation falls and the spacecraft cools; stored energy and thermal control can be needed.

questions.stem: What can interrupt direct communication between an orbiter and Earth?
options: A short period of stored battery power
Deployment of a thermal shield
A change in the spacecraft internal temperature alone
Earth occultation by the target body
questions.explanation: If the target body blocks the line of sight to Earth, direct communication is temporarily interrupted.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of an atmospheric probe released at a planet?
options: Remain permanently in orbit around the planet
Provide launch thrust to the carrier spacecraft
Measure atmospheric conditions during descent
Travel across the solid surface for years
questions.explanation: An instrumented atmospheric probe studies atmospheric conditions as it descends.

questions.stem: Why does an atmospheric entry probe carry a heat shield?
options: To maintain buoyancy after parachute deployment
To protect it from entry heating
To generate thrust for orbital capture
To store radio signals for later transmission
questions.explanation: The shield protects the probe against thermal loads during atmospheric entry.

questions.stem: Which vehicle is designed to drift in an atmosphere while collecting information?
options: An orbiter
An atmospheric balloon
A surface penetrator
A space station
questions.explanation: A balloon floats and drifts in an atmosphere and can return position and atmospheric measurements.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a surface penetrator from a rover?
options: It is designed to travel continuously on the surface
It remains in orbit to map the surface
It floats through the upper atmosphere
It is designed to enter the surface through impact
questions.explanation: A penetrator survives impact and enters the surface to investigate material there; a rover moves over the surface.

questions.stem: Why is semi-autonomous operation useful for a Mars rover?
options: A Mars rover remains within a fixed laboratory
Radio communication travels instantly at every distance
Signals can take minutes to travel between Earth and Mars
A rover never exchanges commands with Earth
questions.explanation: The communication delay makes immediate remote steering impractical, so onboard autonomy can assist operations.

questions.stem: Which description best matches a space station?
options: A vehicle that must pass a target without orbiting it
A spacecraft designed primarily for a single atmospheric descent
An inhabited orbital structure supported by visiting transport vehicles
A surface vehicle designed to penetrate ground on impact
questions.explanation: A space station is designed for habitation in space; visiting spacecraft provide transport to and from it.
